text: The Fed is now signaling potential rate hikes in 2026 instead of cuts, July payrolls unexpectedly fell 23,000, and GDP growth is slowing to 1.5% — this combination of sticky inflation with weakening jobs means the economy is flirting with stagflation, so tighten stops and hold more cash.
Bloom Energy's 37% revenue growth is impressive but at 48x earnings and 31% off its high in a slowing economy with possible rate hikes ahead, trim some exposure to lock in gains and reduce risk.
Adobe at just 9.8x earnings with 10.5% revenue growth and best-in-class free cash flow is genuinely cheap for a software leader — add on this pullback while the value gap is wide.
Meta at 17x earnings with 22% revenue growth and the strongest free cash flow yield among your tech holdings is a quality compounder at a discount — add to this position.
Google at 23.5x earnings with 15% revenue growth and strong cash generation is a reasonable price for a dominant business — add gradually on any further weakness.
